hpi: {{patient_name}} is an elderly patient presenting with the classic triad of normal pressure hydrocephalus: (1) gait disturbance ('magnetic gait' — feet feel stuck to floor), (2) urinary incontinence, and (3) progressive cognitive decline/dementia. NPH is one of the few reversible causes of dementia and must be recognized early. CT/MRI shows ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal atrophy, without obstruction. LP opening pressure is NORMAL (<18 cm H2O) — this distinguishes NPH from obstructive hydrocephalus. High-volume LP (30-50 mL CSF removal) with pre- and post- gait assessment is diagnostic: improvement in gait after CSF removal supports the diagnosis and predicts response to VP shunting. Definitive treatment: ventriculoperitoneal shunt.
